Rashi on Chullin 3a:1:1.hebrew: חרב הרי הוא כחלל - טומאות של מת הראויות לטמא כלי, כגון מת והנוגע בו, דהוי מיהא אב הטומאה, אם נגע בהם מתכות נעשה כיוצא בו, ואם נגע במת הוי אבי אבות [הטומאה], ואם בטמא מת נגע הוי אב, אבל ראשון ושני אין מטמאין כלים, והאי סכין נעשה אב. והאי חרב הרי הוא כחלל, הכא לא איצטריך, דבלאו הכי נמי מצי מטמא בשר, דגברא הוי אב הטומאה וסכין ראשון ובשר שני, אלא רבותא קאמר דאפילו ראשון הוי האי בשר:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:1:1.english: A sword is like a corpse - [This refers to] impurities of a corpse that are capable of imparting impurity to a vessel, such as [the impurity of] a corpse itself, or one who touches it, which is at least a father of impurity (av hatumah): if metal touches them it becomes like it [i.e., attains that same status]; if it touches the corpse [itself] it becomes a "father of fathers of impurity" (avi avot hatumah); and if it touches [a person who is] impure through contact with a corpse, it becomes a father [of impurity] - but a first-degree or second-degree impurity does not impart impurity to vessels. And so this knife becomes a father [of impurity]. Now, [as for the statement that] "a sword is like a corpse" - here it was not [really] necessary, for even without this [law] it could still impart impurity to the meat, since the person is a father of impurity, the knife would [then] be first-degree, and the meat second-degree; rather, [the statement] comes to teach a novel point: that even when [the knife is] only first-degree, this meat also becomes first-degree like it [rather than dropping to second-degree, as would normally happen when a first-degree impurity touches food].

Rashi on Chullin 3a:2:1.hebrew: דאיטמי בשרץ - דהוי האי גברא ראשון, ולא מטמא הסכין, שאין כלי מקבל טומאה אלא מאב הטומאה, דלא מצינו בתורה דמקבל טומאה מראשון ושני אלא אוכל ומשקה, כדכתיב (ויקרא יא) כל אשר בתוכו יטמא, וסמיך ליה מכל האוכל אשר יאכל, אוכלים ומשקים מיטמאים מאויר כלי חרס שהוא ראשון ועושה למה שבתוכו שני, ואין כלי מיטמא מאויר כלי חרס, שאם היה כלי נתון בתוכו ונטמא החיצון, השני טהור, והכי מפרש בשלהי פירקין:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:2:1.english: That he became impure through a sheretz - for this person becomes a rishon (a first-degree impurity), and he does not render the knife impure, since a vessel receives impurity only from an av hatumah (a primary source of impurity). For we do not find in the Torah that anything receives impurity from a rishon or a sheni (a first- or second-degree impurity) except food and drink, as it is written (Leviticus 11): "whatever is inside it shall become impure," and juxtaposed to it: "of all food that may be eaten" - foods and drinks become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel, which is itself a rishon and renders what is inside it a sheni. But a vessel does not become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel, for if a vessel had been placed inside it and the outer one became impure, the inner one remains pure. And this is explained at the end of this chapter.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:2:2.hebrew: קרומית של קנה - פשוטי כלי עץ, ולא מקבלי טומאה:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:2:2.english: The stalk of a reed - [It is] a flat wooden vessel, and [such vessels] do not become susceptible to ritual impurity.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:3:1.english: Abaye endeavors to reconcile [the rulings of] the Mishnah [regarding] ab initio and after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:3:2.hebrew: ואפילו כותי - מוסרין לו בהמה לכתחלה לשחוט, דמצוה שהחזיקו בה היא. אבל ישראל יוצא ונכנס לא ימסור לו לשחוט, דאע"ג דהוחזקו בה לעצמם, אין מקפידין אם יאכלו ישראל נבילות, דלית להו לפני עור לא תתן מכשול (שם יט) אלא כמשמעו, שלא יתן אבן בדרך עור להפילו:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:3:2.english: And even a Samaritan (Kuthite) - One may hand over an animal to him ab initio to slaughter, for [proper] slaughter is a mitzvah that they have taken it upon themselves [to observe]. But an Israelite who goes out and comes in [i.e., one not under constant supervision] - one should not hand [an animal] over to him to slaughter, for even though they have taken it upon themselves [to observe the laws of slaughter] for their own sake, they are not particular about whether [other] Israelites will end up eating unslaughtered carcasses [as a result], since they do not hold that "before a blind person you shall not place a stumbling block" (ibid. 19) [applies] except in its plain sense - that one should not put a stone in a blind person's path to make him fall.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:4:1.hebrew: אכלו מותר לאכול - דהא לעצמו זהיר בה, והיינו דיעבד דמתניתין:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:4:1.english: If he ate it, it is permitted to eat - For he [the Samaritan] is indeed careful about it for himself, and this is the after-the-fact [validation] of our Mishnah.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:5:1.english: Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, for even after the fact it is also not [valid] - for behold, we are indeed dealing with [a case of] after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:5:2.english: Lest they delay - Further on [the Gemara] explains why it uses the future tense.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:7:1.hebrew: אפילו לכתחלה - והכא קתני באחרים, רואין אותם ששחטו, דיעבד:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:7:1.english: Even ab initio - Whereas here [the Mishnah's ruling] speaks of others [who] merely see that they slaughtered - [which validates it] only after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:8:1.hebrew: אמר רבא - והיכא דישראל יוצא ונכנס לא ימסור לכותי לכתחלה, בתמיה:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:8:1.english: Rava said - And [is it really so that] where a Jew goes in and out, he may not entrust [the animal] to a Samaritan ab initio? [This is stated] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:8:2.english: But we learned - In the last chapter of tractate Avodah Zarah, that even though a Jew goes in and out, [the wine] is permitted; this shows that the idolater is afraid lest the Jew come [back], and so he does not touch [the wine]. Here too, [the idolater] is afraid that [the Jew] will now come and see him [in the act].

Rashi on Chullin 3a:8:3.hebrew: מי קתני מניח - אדם עובד כוכבים בחנותו ויוצא ונכנס, דמשמע לכתחלה:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:8:3.english: Does it teach "one leaves"? - [Does the Mishnah word it as:] "A person leaves an idolater in his shop, and [a Jew] goes out and comes in" - which would imply [that this is permitted] ab initio?

Rashi on Chullin 3a:9:1.english: The one who need not [sit and] watch - [need not sit and watch] the wine.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:9:2.hebrew: צריך שיהא יושב ומשמר כו' - רישא אסיפא לא תקשי, דלא זו אף זו קתני, כלומר לא בדיעבד דווקא, אלא אפילו לכתחלה:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:9:2.english: He must be sitting and guarding, etc. - The first clause does not pose a difficulty against the last clause, for it teaches [in the style of] "not only this, but even this" [i.e., in ascending order of novelty]; that is to say, [the leniency stated in the last clause] is not [limited to being valid] specifically after the fact, but [applies] even from the outset.

Tosafot on Chullin 3a:10:1.hebrew: אבל בא ומצאו ששחט חותך כזית בשר ונותן לו - ואם תאמר: כיון דרבא מדמה שחיטה ליין נסך, בא ומצאו לישתרי בלא חותך כזית בשר ונותן לו, כמו ביין נסך דשרי במתניתין בפ' ר' ישמעאל (ע"ז דף ס:) בעובד כוכבים שנמצא בצד הבור, כשאין לו מלוה עליו. וי"ל: כדפרישית לעיל, כיון שיכול לברר על ידי כזית בשר, יש לו לברר:
Tosafot on Chullin 3a:10:1.english: But if he came and found that he had [already] slaughtered, he cuts a piece of meat the size of an olive and gives it to him - And if you should say: since Rava compares slaughtering to [the case of] wine used for idolatrous libation (yayin nesech), [then in the case of] "he came and found him," it should be permitted without [needing to] cut a piece of meat the size of an olive and give it to him - just as, with regard to wine used for idolatrous libation, it is permitted in the Mishnah in the chapter "Rabbi Yishmael" (Avodah Zarah 60b), in the case of an idolater who is found standing beside the pit, when he has no outstanding loan against him. One can say: as I explained above, since he is able to clarify [the matter] by means of [examining] a piece of meat the size of an olive, he is obligated to clarify it.

Tosafot on Chullin 3a:2:1.hebrew: כגון דבדק קרומית של קנה - ואם תאמר: והיאך ישחוט בקרומית של קנה, והא בעינן כלי, כדמוכח בסוף התודה (מנחות דף פב:) ובסוף דם חטאת (זבחים דף צז:), דדריש מדכתיב ויקח את המאכלת לשחוט את בנו דעולה טעונה כלי, וילפינן כולהו מעולה? וי"ל: כגון דתיקנה לקרומית ועשאה כעין כלי. ואע"ג דקיימא לן כרבי דאמר פ' החליל (סוכה דף נ:) אין עושין כלי שרת של עץ, ופליג אר' יוסי בר רבי יהודה דאמר בפרק החליל עושין כלי שרת של עץ - לשחיטת קדשים לא בעינן כלי שרת, דבפרק התודה (מנחות דף עח:) אמרי' דסכין מקדשה ככלי שרת. וכן משמע בתוספתא דקתני: חומר בקמיצה מבשחיטה, שהקמיצה טעונה כלי, והשחיטה אינה טעונה כלי, אלא אפילו קרומית של קנה. ועל כרחך לא בעי למימר דאינה טעונה כלי כלל, דהא ילפינן מעולה דטעונה כלי, אלא דאינה טעונה כלי שרת קאמר. מיהו יש לדחות דלא בעינן כלי יפה קאמר, ולא פסלינן קרומית של קנה משום הקריבהו נא לפחתך (מלאכי א), כדפריך גמרא בסוטה (דף יד:) גבי כפיפה מצרית, דהתם דורון הוא דדרך להביאו בכלי נאה, אבל בשחיטה לא חיישינן. אי נמי כפיפה מצרית מכוערת יותר מקרומית של קנה. ורבינו אפרים היה מביא ראיה מדתנן בפרק איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף מז.): שחיטתן בצפון וקבול דמן בכלי שרת בצפון, ואילו שחיטתן בכלי שרת לא קתני, כדקתני גבי קבלה. ואין זה ראיה, דגבי קבלה נמי לא הזכיר אלא לאשמועינן דבעי שיהא גם הכלי בצפון, לאפוקי אם הכלי בדרום והבהמה בצפון והדם מקלח בתוכו. תדע, דבקדשים קלים דלא בעי צפון לא חש להזכיר קבלה בכלי שרת. ובפ' כל הזבחים שקבל דמן (שם כו.), דתנן: קדשים קלים שחיטתן בפנים וקבול דמן בכלי שרת בפנים - התם נמי אתא לאשמועינן דצריך שיהא הכלי בפנים, לאפוקי אם רוב הכלי בחוץ ומיעוטו בפנים ומקבל הדם במיעוט שבפנים, אע"ג שאין נפסל ביוצא:
Tosafot on Chullin 3a:2:1.english: Such as where he checked the reed-membrane - And if you should say: how can one slaughter with a reed-membrane, when we require a vessel (keli), as is proven at the end of [the chapter] "HaTodah" (Menachot 82b) and at the end of "Dam Chatat" (Zevachim 97b), where it is derived from the verse "and he took the knife to slaughter his son" that an olah (burnt offering) requires a vessel, and we derive all [other sacrifices] from the olah? We may answer: [this is a case] where he fashioned the reed-membrane and made it into something like a vessel. And even though we hold like Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who says in the chapter "HaChalil" (Sukkah 50b) that one may not make sacred service-vessels (klei sharet) of wood - disagreeing with Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda, who says in that same chapter that one may make service-vessels of wood - nevertheless, for the slaughtering of consecrated animals we do not require a service-vessel, for in the chapter "HaTodah" (Menachot 78b) it is said that the knife becomes sanctified like a service-vessel. And so it also appears from the Tosefta, which teaches: there is a stringency in the [handful-]scooping (kemitzah) [of a meal-offering] as compared to slaughter, in that the scooping requires a vessel while the slaughter does not require a vessel - rather, even a reed-membrane [suffices]. And this must mean not that it requires no vessel at all, for we derive from the olah that it requires a vessel, but rather that it does not require a [sanctified] service-vessel. However, one could reject [this], saying it means: we do not require a fine vessel, and we do not disqualify a reed-membrane on account of "offer it, pray, to your governor" (Malachi 1) - as the Gemara in Sotah (14b) raises a difficulty regarding an Egyptian wicker basket (kefifah Mitzrit) - for there it is a gift (doron), and the practice is to bring it in a fine vessel, but with regard to slaughter we are not concerned about this. Alternatively, an Egyptian wicker basket is uglier than a reed-membrane [making it a poor comparison]. And Rabbeinu Ephraim used to bring a proof from what we learn in the chapter "Eizehu Mekoman" (Zevachim 47a): "their slaughter [is performed] in the north, and the receiving of their blood [is performed] in a service-vessel in the north" - whereas it does not teach "their slaughter [is performed] with a service-vessel," as it does teach regarding the receiving [of the blood]. But this is not a proof, for regarding the receiving [of the blood] too, it mentioned [the service-vessel] only to teach us that the vessel must also be in the north - to exclude a case where the vessel is in the south and the animal is in the north, with the blood spurting into it [across the boundary]. You can know this, for regarding lesser consecrated offerings (kodashim kalim), which do not require [slaughter] in the north, it did not trouble to mention receiving [the blood] in a service-vessel. And in the chapter "Kol HaZevachim Shekibel Damam" (ibid. 26a), where we learn: "lesser consecrated offerings - their slaughter [is performed] inside, and the receiving of their blood [is performed] in a service-vessel inside" - there too it came to teach us that the vessel must be inside, to exclude a case where most of the vessel is outside and only a minority is inside, and one receives the blood in the portion that is inside - even though [the offering] is not disqualified by [some blood] going outside.

Tosafot on Chullin 3a:8:1.hebrew: המניח קתני דיעבד - לאו לשנויי אליבא דאביי קאתי, דהא אביי נמי לא שרי בדיעבד בלא חותך כזית בשר, אלא בא להקשות על דברי רבא שמדקדק מכאן דשרי אף לכתחלה. אי נמי, כל זמן שיכול לתקן על ידי חותך כזית בשר יש לו לתקן, אבל אי ליתא לכותי קמן שרי:
Tosafot on Chullin 3a:8:1.english: "One who leaves" is taught as a case after the fact - This does not come to answer according to Abaye's opinion, for Abaye, too, does not permit [the Samaritan's slaughter] after the fact (bediavad) without cutting an olive-bulk (kezayit) of meat [and feeding it to him]. Rather, it comes to pose a difficulty against the statement of Rava, who deduces from here that it is permitted even ab initio (lechatchila). Alternatively: whenever one is able to remedy [the lack of supervision] by cutting an olive-bulk of meat [and giving it to the Samaritan to eat], he must remedy it in that way; but if the Samaritan is no longer there before us [to be given the meat], it is permitted [to eat from his slaughter] regardless.

Tosafot on Chullin 3a:8:2.hebrew: המניח קתני דיעבד - לא בעי למימר דמשמע דיעבד ולא לכתחלה, דהא מסיק דשרי לכתחלה, אלא קאמר דאף דיעבד משמע. וא"ת, דלקמן (חולין דף טו:) גבי השוחט במגל יד, וגבי השוחט אחד בעוף (לקמן חולין דף כז.), דייק השוחט דיעבד אין כו'. וי"ל דאשחיטתן כשרה סמיך התם, דמשמע דיעבד. אבל קשה ממתניתין דהמקנא לאשתו (סוטה דף ב.) ופ' חבית (שבת דף קמז.) גבי הרוחץ במי מערה, דייק בגמרא דיעבד אין לכתחלה לא: [ועיין תוס' סוטה ב. ד"ה המקנא דיעבד]:
Tosafot on Chullin 3a:8:2.english: It teaches "one who leaves [it]," [implying] after the fact - It does not mean to say that this implies [only] after the fact (bediavad) and not ab initio (lechatchila), for it goes on to conclude that it is permitted ab initio; rather, it says that even after the fact, [the wording] implies [validity]. And if you should ask: further on (Chullin 15b), regarding one who slaughters with a hand-sickle, and regarding one who slaughters one [siman] of a bird (below, Chullin 27a), it infers from "one who slaughters": after the fact, yes, etc. [implying not ab initio] - one can answer that there it relies on [the wording] "their slaughter is valid," which implies after the fact. But this is difficult from the Mishnah of "one who is jealous of his wife" (Sotah 2a), and from the chapter "Chavit" (Shabbat 147a), regarding one who washes in cave water, where the Gemara infers: after the fact, yes; ab initio, no. [And see Tosafot on Sotah 2a, s.v. "HaMekaneh" - "bediavad."]

Tosafot on Chullin 3a:9:1.hebrew: אלא מהכא - גרס, ולא גרס מסיפא דהך דהמניח בפ"ב דמסכת ע"ז (דף סט.), וההיא דאין השומר היא בפ' ר' ישמעאל (עבודה זרה סא.):
Tosafot on Chullin 3a:9:1.english: Rather, from here - This is to be read [as a new proof-text], and not read as [continuing] from the end (seifa) of this [Mishnah] of "one who leaves [a gentile in his store]" (HaMani'ach), which is in the second chapter of tractate Avodah Zarah (69a). Rather, that [teaching] of "the guard [need not sit and watch]" is [located] in the chapter of Rabbi Yishmael (Avodah Zarah 61a).

Tosafot on Chullin 3a:9:2.hebrew: אין השומר צריך כו' - משמע הכא דאין צריך משמע לכתחלה, וקשה, דבריש גיטין (דף ד:) גבי הא דאמר רבה לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה, פריך עלה מהא דתנן: "המביא גט ממדינה למדינה במדינת הים, צריך שיאמר בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם", הא באותה מדינה לא צריך. ומשני: לא תימא הא באותה מדינה לא צריך, אלא הא ממדינה למדינה בא"י לא צריך. ופריך: הא בהדיא קתני לה, "המביא גט בא"י אין צריך" כו'. ומשני: אי מההיא ה"א ה"מ דיעבד כו', והיכי ה"א דיעבד, הא אין צריך משמע לכתחלה, כדמשמע הכא. ובקונטרס פי' שם דהכי פריך: הא בהדיא קתני לה, וכיון דאשמועינן לה מדיוקא דרישא, סיפא למאי איצטריך, ומשני: דאי מרישא ה"א דוקא דיעבד, להכי אצטריך סיפא לאשמועינן אפילו לכתחלה. אבל לשון "אי מההיא" לא משמע הכי. וי"ל, דהתם כיון שיכול לתקן בדיעבד, כדקאמר בההוא פרקא (שם ה:) שיטלנו הימנה ויחזור ויתננו לה בפני שנים ויאמר בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, שייך למיתני אין צריך, כלומר אין צריך לחזור וליטול אותו הימנה. א"נ, התם ה"א ה"מ דיעבד, דלכתחלה צריך שיראה כתיבת הגט וחתימה, ואם לא ראה ה"א אין צריך לחזור ולכתוב, אלא יתן לה אע"פ שלא ראה, קמ"ל דלכתחלה נמי אין צריך לראות. ועי"ל, דהכא דייק משום דקאי ארישא דקתני בפ' ר' ישמעאל (ע"ז דף סא.) בעיר שכולה עובדי כוכבים אסור עד שיהא שם שומר, והדר תני אין השומר צריך כו', משמע שבא לפרש דיוצא ונכנס חשיב כשומר גמור, והיינו כשומר דרישא:
Tosafot on Chullin 3a:9:2.english: The guard does not need, etc. - The implication here is that "does not need to" implies [that this applies] even ab initio (lechatchila). But this is difficult, for at the beginning of [tractate] Gittin (4b), regarding Rabbah's statement that [a get requires supervision] because they are not expert in [the requirement of writing it] for her sake (lishmah), the Gemara raises a difficulty from what we learned: "One who brings a get from one province to another overseas (medinat ha-yam) must say, 'In my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed.'" This implies that within the same province he does not need to. And it answers: do not say that [the implication is] within the same province he does not need to; rather, [it means that when bringing a get] from one province to another within Eretz Yisrael, he does not need to. And it objects: but this is taught explicitly - "one who brings a get within Eretz Yisrael does not need to" etc. And it answers: had we [derived this] only from that [explicit teaching], I would have thought it applies only after the fact (bediavad), etc. But how could one have thought [it means only] bediavad? Doesn't "does not need to" imply [that it applies] even ab initio, as it implies here [in our Gemara]? And Rashi explained there that the difficulty is phrased as follows: this is taught explicitly [in the second clause], and since we could already derive it from the precise implication of the first clause (reisha), why is the second clause (seifa) needed at all? And it answers: had we derived it only from the reisha, we would have thought that specifically bediavad [it is permitted]; therefore the seifa was needed to teach that even ab initio [it is permitted]. But the wording "had we [derived it] only from that" does not seem to bear this meaning [since "that" ought to refer to the explicit seifa, not to an inference from the reisha]. And one can answer that there [in the case of a get], since the matter can be rectified after the fact - as is stated in that chapter (Gittin 5b), that he can take the get back from her and give it to her again in front of two witnesses, saying "in my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed" - it is fitting to phrase it as "does not need to," meaning: he does not need to go back and retrieve it from her. Alternatively, there one might have thought that the rule applies only bediavad - that ab initio he must see the writing and signing of the get, and if he did not see it, one might have thought that he need not go back and have it rewritten, but may simply give it to her even though he did not see it - so it teaches that even ab initio he need not see it. And furthermore, one can say that here [in our Gemara] the inference is drawn because it is built upon the reisha, which teaches, in the chapter of Rabbi Yishmael (Avodah Zarah 61a): "In a town populated entirely by idolaters, it is forbidden [to leave one's animal] until a guard is there," and then teaches, "the guard does not need to" etc. - implying that this comes to explain that one who goes in and out is considered a full-fledged guard, which is the same guard mentioned in the reisha.

Rashi on Chullin 3a:13:1.english: Rav Ashi said - He reads [the text as]:

Rashi on Chullin 3a:13:2.hebrew: לתיאבון - כי לא משכח היתר אכיל נבילות, ומאחר שהסכין בדוקה ונתונה בידו שחיט שפיר, דכל כמה דמצי למיכל היתירא לא אכיל איסורא, וכי אין לו סכין בדוק לא טרח להדורי בתר סכין יפה אם זו פגומה:
Rashi on Chullin 3a:13:2.english: For appetite - Because if he cannot find permitted [meat], he eats [non-kosher] carcasses. And since the knife is checked [to be flawless] and placed in his hand, he slaughters properly, for as long as he is able to eat permitted [meat], he will not eat forbidden [meat]. But when he does not have a checked knife, he does not trouble himself to go searching for a good knife if this one is flawed.
